body:
If I remember right, this is intentional (if not altogether obvious from your debug usage).
See #94413 .

If you look in `Input::action_press()`:
```
// As input may come in part way through a physics tick, the earliest we can react to it is the next physics tick.
action_state.pressed_physics_frame = Engine::get_singleton()->get_physics_frames() + 1;
```

The reason for this is as the comment. There is a point at which the physics tick counter rolls over to the next tick, this occurs at the _start_ of each iteration.

We have 3 requirements:
* we want to react to input as quickly as possible
* we don't want to miss any input
* we don't want to react to any input twice

If we set the action tick on `action_press()` to the current tick, then it works for your MRP, but the problem is that other scripts may run before yours, won't see the action (because it hasn't been pressed yet), see #94039. On the next tick they also won't see the action, because the tick has expired (it is now at tick+1).

So in order to ensure all scripts etc have a chance to react to an action that is pressed _within_ a tick (without missing it), the earliest we can schedule it is _the next tick_.

Another alternative is to allow the action to be considered _just pressed_ for the current tick _and_ the next. But the problem here is that the action will be just pressed _twice_.

(_We did consider options of being able to retire just pressed actions after the first detection to prevent detection twice, but a user could call `is_action_just_pressed()` on the same action from multiple scripts, and expect it to work, thus would be compat breaking._)

In 99.9% of situations the current behaviour is exactly what you want, but it has the side effect if you programmatically call press as in your MRP, it won't appear until the next tick.

_There probably are alternative ways of approaching the just pressed problem, but this is the one we've currently gone with._

### A quirk
A quirk of this, is that if you are really sneaky, you could theoretically get faster input reaction by checking for the first `pressed` state yourself rather than relying on `is_action_just_pressed()`. This is only theoretical though, as on most platforms the input is detected once before any of the ticks run, so there would be no difference.

Android afaik is the only platform that currently runs threaded input that could benefit from reaction _within_ a tick.

I would have expected to get something like this:
```gdscript
-1 pressed = false
0 pressed = false
1 pressed = true just_pressed = true
2 pressed = true
3 pressed = true
4 pressed = true
5 pressed = true
6 pressed = true
7 pressed = true
8 pressed = true
9 pressed = true
10 pressed = true
11 pressed = false just_released = true
12 pressed = false
```
Instead of just pressed and just released being 1 tick earlier I would have expected pressed to be 1 tick delayed. This would ensure that pressed and just pressed/just released are never out of sync and should avoid the risk of scripts missing just pressed inputs.

In fact if you use Input.parse_input_event then this is the exact behavior you get. I think it would be good to match that.

Yes, obviously if this can be achieved (while meeting existing contracts) it would be great.
It isn't super obvious how to do this - but PRs / proposals are always welcome.
